extracted.intended_audience: environmental journalists, reporters, and prospective SEJ members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards from the Society of Environmental Journalists about what topics, newsworthiness drivers, reporting practices, and quality criteria define strong environmental journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEJ membership eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on who qualifies for SEJ membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active members: editorially independent journalism, no paid lobbying/PR on environment; Associate: must spend more time on journalism than environmental PR; Lobbyists/PR pros: NOT eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate change
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a primary topic area for environmental journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among SEJ topic areas indicating a core beat for coverage (climate's long-term consequences and gradual nature are emphasized elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollution (air, water, soil)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pollution of air, water, and soil is a core topic area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often tied to public health implications and toxics/chemical exposure reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species extinction / biodiversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of species loss and biodiversity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects to species iconography and conservation topics; may involve scientific findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land use / habitat
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on land-use changes and habitat issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links local impacts to broader ecological or policy systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy (oil, gas, renewables, nuclear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy sector reporting across fossil fuels and renewables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can implicate corporate accountability, government regulation, and climate consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildfires / extreme weather
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of wildfires and extreme weather events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to disaster-scale reporting and linking events to climate and local impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality / quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on water-related issues including scarcity and contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often intersects with public health, regulatory accountability, and community impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxics / chemical exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of toxic substances and chemical exposure risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strongly tied to public health implications and investigative work on responsible actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on disproportionate environmental impacts on marginalized communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized as a newsworthiness driver and part of quality reporting: engage historically marginalized communities and highlight disproportionate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous land rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of Indigenous rights and land issues in environmental contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires attention to community voices, history, and legal/political contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecology / wildlife
rubrics_metrics.description: General ecology and wildlife reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can include scientific findings, species-focused stories, and conservation angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation / parks
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of conservation efforts and protected areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May involve investigative reporting on policy and management, and human/community angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural / food systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on agriculture, food production, and related environmental impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects to toxics, land use, water, and public health angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: does the story implicate human health (e.g., pollution, toxics)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories with clear public health consequences are prioritized; quantitative literacy and scientific accuracy are expected when discussing health impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: does the issue have long-term or systemic consequences (e.g., climate change)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should provide long-term context and avoid treating gradual processes as non-newsworthy; connect slow-moving trends to tangible impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local impact of global issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: showing how global problems affect local communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that tie local consequences to broader global trends increase relevance and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: does the story hold polluters or corporations responsible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate corporate records and name responsible actors when appropriate; follow-the-money and ownership/operations scrutiny are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: scrutiny of regulators, enforcement, and policy decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative reporting into government records, enforcement lapses, and regulatory choices is prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice as driver
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: highlighting disproportionate impacts on marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage historically marginalized communities and reflect their perspectives; avoid erasing inequities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species iconography (charismatic wildlife)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: stories about charismatic species that attract public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use species stories to illuminate larger ecological or policy issues, not merely spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: the scale and severity of natural or human-caused disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale events or disasters merit coverage but should be contextualized with causes, consequences, and human stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: reporting on peer-reviewed science and new research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scientific accuracy, quantitative literacy, and long-term context; avoid false balance regarding climate denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human stories of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness driver: individual or community narratives illustrating broader issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell human stories that illuminate systems and connect to larger environmental themes without sensationalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry-funded sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standard: avoid reliance on industry-funded sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek independence to prevent conflicts of interest; be wary of industry PR shaping the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standard: include a mix of community, scientific, and regulatory sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify voices to provide context and counterbalance single-source narratives; center affected communities where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term context required
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standard: place issues in historical and longer-term context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain trends over time, not just immediate events; connect present developments to past policies and likely futures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative literacy expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standard: ability to understand and use quantitative data appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should interpret data correctly, explain uncertainties, and avoid misleading statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding false balance for climate denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standard: do not present climate denial as equivalently valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving undue credibility to denialist positions; reflect scientific consensus and weight of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow news problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: climate and environmental issues often evolve slowly and lack immediate dramatic events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must find angles that make long-term processes newsworthy by connecting to immediate impacts and human stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: many environmental phenomena (e.g., greenhouse gases) are invisible and hard to visualize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use creative visualization and clear explanation to make abstract environmental concepts tangible for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: audiences may be fatigued by recurring or alarming environmental stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance tone to avoid alarmism; focus on agency, solutions, and human-scale narratives to maintain engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry pushback
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: reporters may face opposition or pushback from industry actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for pushback by documenting records, sourcing carefully, and anticipating counterclaims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source intimidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: sources (especially vulnerable communities) may be intimidated or fearful of speaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect sources, build trust, and use culturally appropriate practices to ensure voices are heard safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-science attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct challenge: targeted attacks on scientific findings or experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defend scientific accuracy through transparent sourcing, context, and explanation of methods and consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEJ Annual Conference & Awards as standard of excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit recognition mechanism: SEJ's awards and conference recognize excellence in environmental journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards signal implicit definitions of best work: rigorous reporting, investigative depth, community engagement, and storytelling that meets the standards above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connects local to global
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: strong work links local impacts to global systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how local stories reflect larger trends, policies, or global processes to increase relevance and explanatory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names responsible actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: identify the corporations, agencies, or parties responsible for environmental harms or decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about culpability and chain of responsibility; use records and documentation when naming actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides scientific accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: ensure factual and scientific correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer-reviewed research, expert sources, and quantitative literacy; avoid false balance and misrepresentation of uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engages historically marginalized communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: center and include voices from marginalized populations affected by environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively reach out to and represent these communities, respecting context, agency, and lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigates corporate/government records
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: use document-based investigative methods to uncover accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine records, enforcement histories, and corporate filings to substantiate claims and reveal systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tells human stories within larger systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: use individual narratives to illuminate systemic causes and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing stories to individual anecdotes; connect personal experiences to policy, corporate, and ecological contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids both alarmism and denialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit quality criterion: strike a balance between sensationalism and minimizing the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sober, accurate reporting that communicates risk without exaggeration and reflects the scientific consensus.
